articles.author: Chris Townsend
articles.content_excerpt: By Chris Townsend October 9, 2026 PART ONE Few in the United States would know the true history of relations between our country and the Caribbean nation of Cuba. The United States seized Cuba during the Spanish-American War of 1898. A brief, opportunist war triggered by the U.S. on flimsy pretexts to grab several valuable pieces of the decaying Spanish Empire. In addition to Cuba and the Philippines, the islands Puerto Rico and Guam were quickly subjugated by the U.S. military in the conflict. National liberation movements of varying strengths had been operating in all of Spain’s possessions, but only Cuba was granted its independence in 1902.
